Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::timeline¶

Back to Timeline Index Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

const Timeline& Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::timeline() const

What It Does¶

Returns the underlying 1D Timeline payload without stripping away the temporal values.

Use this when your next operation is not “index semantics” but “general temporal semantics”: formatting, field extraction, timezone conversion, rounding, or other Timeline-native transforms.

In practice, timeline() is the escape hatch from the index surface back to the broader time object.

That is usually the right move when the next step is about what each timestamp is, rather than where it sits on an ordered axis.

Returns¶

const Timeline& A reference to the underlying 1D temporal payload.

Examples¶

Example 1. Expose the full time axis as a 1D Timeline.

auto idx = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:20:00Z",
}).index();

auto axis = idx.timeline();
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(axis) << "\n";

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[5], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-11-01 00:00:00, 2024-11-01 00:20:00, 2024-11-01 00:40:00, 2024-11-01 01:00:00, 2024-11-01 01:20:00 ]

Example 2. Drop to Timeline semantics, do a transform there, then rebuild an index if you need ordered lookup semantics again.

auto local_axis = idx.timeline().floor("H");
auto local_idx = local_axis.index();
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(local_axis) << "\n";
std::cout << "ordered=" << std::boolalpha
          << local_idx.is_monotonic_increasing() << "\n";

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[5], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-11-01 00:00:00, 2024-11-01 00:00:00, 2024-11-01 00:00:00, 2024-11-01 01:00:00, 2024-11-01 01:00:00 ]
ordered=true

Notes¶

  • timeline() does not copy the time values by itself; it exposes the stored payload.

  • The returned object is still 1D because Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor itself is 1D.

  • Staying on Timeline makes sense for formatting, calendar extraction, timezone transforms, and temporal arithmetic.

  • If you need ordered lookup again after a Timeline transformation, rebuild a Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor from the transformed timeline.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::searchsorted: ordered insertion lookup on the index axis.

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::slice_time: label-based time slicing without dropping down to Timeline.
